causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand at 2.30 pm was 10,323 MW which was 695 MW higher than forecast one hour prior.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: Rooftop solar output dropped from over 5,000 MW at midday to around 3,000 MW at 2.30 pm when the high prices occurred.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Wind output was even lower at the time of the high prices, averaging 587 MW during the high price period, which equates to around 20% of the installed capacity in NSW.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: An unplanned network outage on the Lower Tumut to Yass line in southern NSW also contributed to the high prices by limiting access to low-priced generation from southern NSW and Victoria.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: During the high prices, around 800 MW of gas units could not start up quickly enough, and a further 800 MW from units already running could not ramp up quickly enough to mitigate the high prices.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: On this day, for one of the two high-priced 5-minute intervals, at 2.10 pm, offers of around $17,500 per MW in lower FCAS contributed to setting the energy price in NSW.

interconnectors_named.name: Terranora interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: An unplanned outage of all three Directlink cables on the Terranora interconnector since 26 December also limited flows on the interconnector to around 18 MW into NSW.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: This was due to the outage creating a credible risk of losing QNI.

intervals.quote: On 15 January, the 30-minute price in NSW reached $5,906 per MWh at 2.30 pm.
